summary: Full-project static security audit found a blocker symlink-containment defect across MCP resources and harness wiki/skill readers, plus a major unauthenticated non-loopback MCP HTTP configuration gap. Dependency audit reports 28 advisories, but runtime reachability was not established. Platform restrictions prevented live reproduction and additional security tests.

artifacts.summary: Russian full-project security audit with findings, defensive posture and limitations.

findings.problem: MCP resources and harness wiki/skill readers use lexical path containment before file reads, so a symlink can resolve outside the permitted root.
findings.impact: An untrusted repository can cause local host files to be read and returned as project context; MCP resource output also bypasses tool-output redaction.
findings.suggested_fix: Canonicalize root and target with realpath through the existing contained-path helper, require a regular contained file, add symlink regression tests, and apply redaction to resource output.
findings.evidence: Site-check of src/mcp/resources.ts:168-217, src/mcp/dispatch.ts:82-117, and src/harness/tool/metaproject-adapter.ts:141-175,214-252,417-429,627-650; correct contrasting implementation at src/lib/contained-path.ts:78-105.

class_scope.enumeration_method: keryx ctx rg over readFile, resolveConfined, confineToWiki and realpath in MCP resources and the metaproject adapter, followed by reading every matching reader and dispatcher.

findings.problem: The unauthenticated MCP HTTP bridge is described as localhost-only, but its configuration accepts any host and startup binds it without a loopback check.
findings.impact: With the explicit HTTP capability and launch opt-ins enabled, a project configuration can expose project resources and HTTP-unguarded tools to unauthenticated network clients.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject non-loopback MCP hosts or require serve-equivalent external-bind acknowledgement and bearer authentication; enforce an HTTP tool allowlist and path containment centrally.
findings.evidence: Site-check of src/mcp/config.ts:72-82, src/mcp/server.ts:136-153, src/mcp/transport/http-sse.ts:21-45, src/mcp/dispatch.ts:103-117 and src/mcp/tools.ts:549-568. No listener was started.

class_scope.enumeration_method: keryx ctx rg for mergeMcpConfig, HTTP transport declarations, localhost claims, transport guards and mutating registry entries across src/mcp, followed by reading all matches.

findings.problem: The installed dependency tree reports 28 known advisories, including one critical and thirteen high, but vulnerable API reachability was not established.
findings.impact: Development model tooling and optional MCP runtime dependencies may expose denial-of-service, code-generation, parsing or host-confusion weaknesses if affected APIs receive attacker-controlled input.
findings.suggested_fix: Update compatible dependency versions, regenerate the lockfile, rerun audit, and trace production-only reachability for the MCP SDK dependency tree.
